newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM assures Mahathir investments safe.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM assures Mahathir investments safe.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen has written to Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad to condemn the recent annulment by his rival and partner in power of several agreements with a Malaysian firm.

In a letter that revealed bitter differences in the two leaders' stance on the government's deals with its largest investor, Ariston Sdn Bhd, Hun Sen wrote he was "disappointed and shocked" by Co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh's decision to declare three agreements with Ariston "null and void."
Ariston, Hun Sen wrote, had become a victim of politics and irresponsible behavior by Ranariddh.
The deals were still legitimate, he assured Mahathir.

"The Head of State of a country cannot unilaterally make such a hasty and thoughtless decision without going through the proper legal (and) judicial procedures," said the letter, dated March 17 and obtained by Reuters on Friday.
Hun Sen was referring to a February 26 letter that Ranariddh wrote to Ariston Chief Executive Officer Chen Lip Keong.

Ranariddh had written that the Malaysian company's deals to lease land for a large resort and an 18-hole golf course and an airport concession agreement were "null and void" because they were improperly signed by a rival politician.
The agreements were part of Ariston's $1.3 billion plan to develop the southern town of Sihanoukville into a major tourist destination.
Ranariddh's letter reflected continuing tensions between himself and Hun Sen, who formed an uneasy coalition following U.N.-sponsored polls in 1993.
It also increased investor concerns about being caught in the middle of Cambodia's divisive political scene.
Hun Sen acknowledged the problems in his letter, noting, "I must admit that the Royal Government now has some domestic problems which have unfortunately victimised Ariston."
In an apparent effort to resolve the two leaders' differences, officials from Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party were in Sihanoukville on Friday to meet with Ariston representatives, officials said.
But Sun Chanthol, secretary general of the Council for the Development of Cambodia, the investment arm of the government, said he believed the dispute would be resolved soon.
"Cambodia is still a good place to invest... If investors follow the law of the land, they will be protected."
